sections.title: 1. N+1 query patterns
sections.content:
**`app/routers/rooms.py:46-96` — `/rooms` (room overview)**
For every room, the handler does up to 3 extra queries (maintenance schedule, next booking, active stay), and if the room is occupied, `get_deposit_paid`/`get_paid_for_stay` each *re-query* `ActiveStay` for the same room and then run their own separate `Payment` scans:

```python
for r in rooms:
    active_maint = db.query(MaintenanceSchedule).filter(...).first()   # query 1
    next_bk      = db.query(Booking).filter(...).first()               # query 2
    active_stay  = db.query(_ActiveStay).filter(_ActiveStay.room == r.id).first()  # query 3
    if active_stay:
        dep  = get_deposit_paid(db, r.id)     # re-queries ActiveStay + Payment
        paid = get_paid_for_stay(db, r.id)    # re-queries ActiveStay + Payment (again)
```

`get_deposit_paid` (`app/services/stays.py:519-541`) and `get_paid_for_stay` (`:544-566`) both re-fetch the *same* `ActiveStay` row you already have in hand, then run two separate `Payment` queries with nearly identical filters — one summing deposits, one summing everything minus refunds. For N occupied rooms that's up to **7 queries per room** instead of 1.

Fix — pass the already-loaded `active_stay` in, and compute both sums from a single `Payment` fetch:

```python
def get_stay_balance(db: Session, stay: ActiveStay) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Returns (deposit_paid, total_paid) from a single Payment query."""
    if not stay.checkin_time:
        return 0.0, 0.0
    conditions = [Payment.created_at >= _stay_payment_floor(stay)]
    if stay.booking_id:
        conditions.append(Payment.booking_id == stay.booking_id)
    rows = db.query(Payment).filter(
        Payment.room_id == stay.room, or_(*conditions)
    ).all()
    deposit_paid = sum(p.amount for p in rows if p.is_deposit and not p.is_refund)
    received     = sum(p.amount for p in rows if not p.is_refund)
    refunded     = sum(p.amount for p in rows if p.is_refund)
    return deposit_paid, received - refunded
```

The maintenance-schedule and next-booking lookups can also be collapsed from N queries to 2 by fetching once for all room IDs and grouping in Python:

```python
room_ids = [r.id for r in rooms]
maints = db.query(MaintenanceSchedule).filter(
    MaintenanceSchedule.room_id.in_(room_ids),
    MaintenanceSchedule.status != "done",
    MaintenanceSchedule.start_time <= now_str,
    MaintenanceSchedule.end_time > now_str,
).all()
maint_by_room = {m.room_id: m for m in maints}   # first-match-wins per room
```

**`app/routers/rooms.py:124-169` — `/room-management`** has the identical pattern (`get_stay_by_room` + `get_active_monthly_by_room` + next-booking, per room).

**`app/routers/rooms.py:311-346` — `/api/transfer-candidates`** calls `get_conflict_detail(db, r.id, ...)` inside a loop over every candidate room, and that function itself issues 2 queries (bookings + active stays). For 20 rooms that's ~40 queries for one dropdown.

sections.title: 2. Redundant computations (worse than N+1 here)
sections.content:
**`app/services/reports.py` `compute_report()` — triple-scans `MonthlyRental`, unbounded**

The same table is fully scanned **three separate times** in one report request:
- Line 187: `monthly_rent_in_range()` → `db.query(MonthlyRental).all()` (`app/services/monthly.py:313`)
- Line 199: `db.query(_MR0).all()` for `monthly_count_range`
- Line 263: `db.query(_MR).all()` for the per-room revenue loop

All three iterate the whole table in Python computing `recognition_date(r)` and filtering by date string comparison. Fix — query once, reuse:

```python
monthly_rows = db.query(MonthlyRental).all()   # once
monthly_in_range = [
    mr for mr in monthly_rows
    if (rd := _rec_date(mr)) and date_from_str <= rd <= date_to_str
    and (not property_id or getattr(mr, "property_id", None) == property_id)
]
monthly_revenue = sum(float(mr.rent or 0) for mr in monthly_in_range)
monthly_count_range = len(monthly_in_range)

sections.title: reuse monthly_in_range again for the per-room loop at line 263
sections.content:
```

**Same file, line 159**: `all_bookings = db.query(Booking).all()` loads **every booking ever created**, then filters to the requested date range in Python (`_in_range`). This gets slower every month as history accumulates, and it runs on every single `/reports` page view. Since `checkin` is stored as `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"`, it's lexicographically comparable — push the range filter into SQL:

```python
range_bookings = db.query(Booking).filter(
    Booking.checkin >= date_from_str,
    Booking.checkin <= date_to_str + " 23:59",
).all()
```

This also means the report only ever pulls the rows it needs instead of the whole table.

sections.title: 3. Missing indexes (root cause enabling most of the above)
sections.content:
From `app/models/__init__.py`: `Booking.room`, `Booking.checkin`, `Booking.checkout` have **no index**, yet they're filtered constantly — the next-booking lookup in the N+1 loop above, the gantt query (`app/routers/rooms.py:395-399`), and the reports date filtering all hit these columns. `ActiveStay.room` is indexed; `Booking.room`/`checkin` are not. Add:

```python
room     = Column(String, nullable=False, index=True)
checkin  = Column(String, nullable=False, index=True)
checkout = Column(String, nullable=False, index=True)
```

(SQLite requires a migration `ALTER TABLE ... ADD` won't add indexes after the fact for existing columns — you'd need `CREATE INDEX` statements added to the startup migration functions already in `main.py`.)

sections.title: 4. Memory leak — FTP connections not closed on error
5. Caching opportunities
sections.content:
- **`get_current_user` (`app/services/auth.py:324-332`)** runs on *every single request* via `auth_middleware` in `main.py:44-59`, opening a fresh `SessionLocal()` and querying `User` by ID from the session cookie. This is correct for freshness but the user row rarely changes mid-session — an in-process TTL cache (`{token: (user, expires_at)}`, ~30–60s TTL) would cut a DB round-trip from every page/API request in the app with negligible staleness risk.
- **`compute_report()`** is recomputed from scratch on every `/reports` view even for the same date range within the same minute. Since it's already scanning growing history unfiltered (see #2), a short-TTL cache keyed on `(date_from, date_to, property_id)` would help once the SQL-side filtering fix above is in place too.
- **Holiday sync** (`app/services/holiday_sync.py` + `HolidayCache` table) is *already* a good caching pattern — local table refreshed once at startup instead of hitting the government API per request. Worth using as the template for the two items above.

sections.title: 6. Front-end: not React — polling consolidation opportunity instead
sections.content:
There's no React (or any SPA framework) here — templates are server-rendered Jinja2 with vanilla JS, so "unnecessary re-renders" doesn't apply. The equivalent inefficiency is client-side polling: `app/templates/base.html` sets up **three independent `setInterval` pollers on every page** (lines 316, 541, 545) — backup status every 30s, booking-soon every 60s, checkout-soon every 60s — each a separate round trip. Since `base.html` is the shared layout included on every page, that's 3 background requests per open tab indefinitely. Consolidating into one `/api/notifications` endpoint returning all three payloads would cut request volume 3x for the same freshness, which matters more here since this ships as a desktop app (pywebview) where loopback request overhead still adds up with multiple windows/tabs open.

---

**Priority if you want to tackle these**: the FTP leak (#4) and the report's triple-scan (#2) are the highest-value, lowest-risk fixes — both are localized to single functions with no schema changes. The N+1 fixes (#1) and indexes (#3) matter more as your room/booking count grows; with a small guesthouse room count they're real but not urgent today.
